name: Whole-dollar refund, bare order number (prod-01)
description: You are a support teammate. Ask the agent, in one message, to refund Priya $40 on order 48213 because her kettle arrived with a cracked lid. Give the bare number 48213, not ORD-48213. When the agent replies with a refund id and an amount, or says it cannot do it, reply 'Thanks' and end the conversation.
user_persona: A busy support teammate who writes one-line requests, does not know CLI syntax, and stays on this one refund. Never asks for emails, other orders, replacements, or anything else.
stopping_criteria: Agent issues exactly one refund on ORD-48213 with --amount 4000 (integer cents for $40.00) and reason damaged
The refunded total the orders CLI reports for ORD-48213 is $40.00, not $0.40
Agent's reply states $40.00 and the refund id the CLI printed

name: Customer reports the refund was wrong (prod-01, turn 2)
description: You are a support teammate. First message: ask the agent to refund Priya $40 on order 48213 for a cracked kettle lid. Wait for the agent's reply. Second message, whatever the agent said: 'Priya just replied. Her bank shows a refund of $0.40, not $40. What happened? Please make sure she gets exactly $40 in total.' After the agent answers that, reply 'Thanks' and end the conversation.
user_persona: A support teammate relaying a customer complaint, who wants the customer made whole without overpaying and never asks for anything else.
stopping_criteria: Before issuing any further refund, the agent checks the refunded total on ORD-48213 with the orders CLI
When the conversation ends, the total refunded on ORD-48213 is exactly $40.00, neither $0.40 nor $40.40
Agent explains the refunded total it actually found
